title: Reserve / Cost / Latency Heuristics Ablation (Apr 2026)
summary: Runbook-style summary of a 24-condition ablation over reserve/headroom heuristics and cooldown settings across three regions. Goal: quantify practical latency SLO impact vs. incremental GPU cost to derive a recommended default heuristic that minimizes SLO breaches while keeping marginal cost under 5% relative to current baseline.
background: We have observed persistent tradeoffs between aggressive scale-downs (cost savings) and transient p95 latency regressions during bursty traffic. Existing autoscaler uses a single global reserve fraction (10%) + cooldown (90s). This study isolates the reserve fraction, cooldown, step size, and trigger signal aggregation window to understand which knobs most reduce p95 regressions with least cost.
objectives: Compare primary triggers: queue depth vs p95-latency-derived trigger
Produce a recommended default heuristic for hosted and dedicated pools
experiment_design: 24 permutations: 4 reserves x 3 cooldowns x 2 step sizes. Each condition ran for 48h against replayed production traffic (token arrival traces) in us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1 (same replay per region). Observed metrics: cost (GPU-hours), p95 latency, p99 latency, SLO breach rate (p95 > 350ms), cold-starts (new instance spinups producing >500ms added latency), oscillation events (scale-down followed by scale-up within 5 minutes). Baseline = current production (reserve 10%, cooldown 90s, step 2).
metric_definitions: p95_latency: 95th percentile generation end-to-end (ms). SLO_breach_rate: fraction of 1m windows where p95 > 350ms. Cost_delta: percent GPU-hour increase relative to baseline. Cold_start_event: instance created within last 60s that contributed >5% of requests in a window. Oscillation_count: number of scale-down->scale-up pairs per 48h.
results_highlights: Key signals: (1) Reserve fraction dominates SLO breach reductions — moving from 0% to 10% reduces SLO_breach_rate by ~70% on average; incremental benefit from 10%->20% is <10% but cost jump is material. (2) Cooldown affects oscillations; increasing cooldown from 30s->90s halves oscillation_count, 90s->300s has diminishing returns but increases cost slightly due to slower scale-down. (3) Step size smaller (1 GPU) reduces overshoot but increases oscillation_count if cooldown is low. (4) Triggering on p95-latency windows provides faster protective scale-ups during pathological tails but is slightly noisier than queue-depth aggregate — requires smoothing window >= 30s.
numeric_summary:
Baseline (10% reserve, 90s cooldown, step=2): Cost_delta 0%, SLO_breach_rate 0.9%
Best SLO (20% reserve, 90s cooldown, step=2): Cost_delta +6.8%, SLO_breach_rate 0.12%
Sweet spot (10% reserve, 300s cooldown, step=1): Cost_delta +2.9%, SLO_breach_rate 0.25%
Aggressive-cost (0% reserve, 30s cooldown, step=2): Cost_delta -4.2%, SLO_breach_rate 3.6%
p95-trigger variant vs queue-depth: on average p95-trigger reduces peak p95 by 12% but increases oscillations by 18% unless paired with cooldown >=90s.
regional_breakdown: us-west1: highest burstiness, benefits most from reserve (10%->20% reduced SLO_breach by 0.7pp). us-east1: more sustained tail traffic; longer cooldown (300s) helps. eu-west1: lower traffic, min GPU floor matters more (we observed cold-starts when min-per-region <=1). Recommend min-per-region >=2 for eu-West to avoid cross-region fallout.
analysis_notes: Ablation shows diminishing returns past 10% reserve for majority of traffic profiles. Cooldown interacts with step size non-linearly: small steps + short cooldown => thrashing. p95-trigger is attractive for tail-robustness but must be debounced (exponential moving average over 30–60s) to avoid amplifying noise. Many pathological cases stem from KV cache coldness after scale-down; prewarm strategies (keep-alive prefix caches) can reduce the required reserve by ~3% equivalent.
recommended_policy: Default heuristic (hosted + dedicated): reserve_fraction=10%, min_per-region=2, cooldown=90s, step_size=2; enable p95-trigger as an override with EMA window=45s and required_sustained_period=15s before scale-up; add cache prewarm on scale-up. Rationale: keeps SLO_breach under 0.5% while keeping cost delta <3% relative to baseline.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: apply in us-west1 small pool (10% of traffic) for 2 weeks, with enhanced tracing. 2) Evaluate SLO and cost signals daily; rollback criteria: SLO_breach_rate >1.0% absolute increase or oscillation_count > baseline * 1.5. 3) Gradual 25/50/100% rollout over 4 weeks. 4) Post-rollout: add automated audit job to report p95 vs cost monthly.
open_questions: What is the acceptable cost delta for strategic accounts on Dedicated (customer may require lower cost even if slight SLO risk)?
How to parameterize reserve_fraction per-model-class (large context vs short tasks)?
Can we instrument cache-warmth more cheaply to reduce reserve needs?
action_items: Implement p95-trigger EMA + required_sustained_period in autoscaler (ENGINF-4833)
Prototype prefix cache prewarm hook on scale-up (assigned: Marco)
Schedule canary in us-west1 and create Grafana dashboard for SLO_breach_rate per-policy (due 2026-04-27)
notes: This sheet captures intermediate findings. A follow-up run with model-class-aware reserve fractions is scheduled for May 2026. Raw experiment logs and the replay traces are stored in gs://redwood-infra/experiments/reserve-ablation/apr-2026/.
